text:
The Canucks arrive in Philadelphia with almost nothing going right. They lost 5-1 in Detroit on Wednesday, they're 2-3-0 in their last five and outscored 21-12, and Elias Pettersson is out with an upper-body injury after 23 points in 24 games. The Province reported he was due to see a specialist on this road trip, and ESPN's estimated return is Dec. 4. Brock Boeser has taken his spot beside Jake DeBrusk and Jonathan Lekkerimäki, and Marco Rossi has jumped onto the first power-play unit, up to 17:14 a night. Boeser is also the name in the trade chatter, with The Province writing that he "enters trade chat" during what BVM Sports calls a career year.

The deeper problem in Vancouver is in net and in its own end. The Canucks have taken 41% of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and their goaltending has allowed 13.8 more goals than the shots deserved. Leevi Meriläinen, our projected starter, is at .885. Our numbers give them a 0.1% chance at the playoffs.

The Flyers aren't comfortable either. A three-game winning streak ended in a 7-3 loss in Washington, and Dan Vladar has been rough lately: .850 and 4.1 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Questions about Travis Konecny's commitment have been in the air, which Yahoo Sports argued he shouldn't have to face, and Denver Barkey has become the feel-good story at center with 8 points in his last ten, backed by real chances.

Our numbers see a lopsided night on paper: 3.73 expected goals for Philadelphia, 2.44 for Vancouver. Konecny sits at 30% to score. Our sleepers are both Flyers: Noah Cates (19% to score) and Porter Martone, who moved up beside Barkey and Owen Tippett and is 45% for a point. They met on Nov. 9, a 3-1 Philadelphia win that was a coin flip on chances.
headline: Two teams in a bad mood meet in Philadelphia
